proof:
The actual star and cap family are those in dad8b277ce2587c7, since $l_i(y_a)=a_i-1/(d+1)$ and the sum of thresholds is one. Its proof identifies the actual fibers, strict midpoint compatibility, the maximum raw depth and the cap mass. In particular the body is centrally symmetric and every through-origin cap with nonzero continuous normal has zero boundary mixed volume. Reflection gives exact half mass for every such cap.

Fix $i$ and let $S_i$ and $g_i$ be the positive proper coarea mass and physical centroid on $K\cap\{\lambda_i=a_i\}$. The proper coarea is the area divided by $\|l_i\|$, where the norm denotes that of the linear functional's gradient. On the fiber at $-1$ the coarea force relative to $q(-1)=y_a$ is $S_i(g_i-y_a)$. Reflection $x\mapsto-x$ preserves section area and the norm factor and takes that fiber's section to the section at $1$. The corresponding displacement force is its negative. The middle section of $K-K$ is centrally symmetric about zero, so its force is zero. Likewise the full continuous first moments cancel and the base moments are $-S_i+S_i=0$. The section centroid has coordinates $a_i$ at $i$ and $(1-a_i)/d$ elsewhere, so if all the endpoint section centroids coincided with $y_a$, equality of the coordinates off each index would force $a$ to be canonical. These sections are all proper, including the middle cut through its interior origin.

For minimality, at base zero take a sufficiently small positive multiple of the $i$th centered vertex $v_i$ of $K$. It lies in the interior of $K-K$. Since $l_i(v_i)=d/(d+1)>0$ and $l_j(v_i)=-1/(d+1)<0$ for $j\ne i$, it belongs strictly to precisely the $i$th cap. Every group member is therefore necessary on the actual source. Finally any perturbed margins $\widetilde u_i\cdot(x+z\widetilde y)$ keep a whole-space cover when the continuous normals remain sufficiently close, by the positive-span argument in the common-section cover lemma. These caps still pass through the origin and remain nonvertical, so reflection makes every mass exactly constant.

statement: Let $K$ be a centered $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/(d+1)$. In the compatible reflected star with actual fibers $K,K-K,-K$ at $-1,0,1$, take any strictly positive threshold vector $a$ of sum one and let $y_a$ have barycentric coordinates $a$. The $d+1$ caps with margins $l_i(x+z y_a)$ form an inclusion-minimal whole-space cover of the actual mixed source. Each has mass equal to the attained maximum raw depth $M/2$. At the two endpoint bases, each cap's displacement forces relative to $q(z)=-zy_a$ are exact opposites and its middle displacement force is zero. Its global continuous and base coarea first moments are both zero. If the threshold vector is noncanonical, some individual endpoint section centroid differs from its meeting point despite this global cancellation. All through-origin nonvertical caps have mass $M/2$, including small cover-preserving motions of the group and its affine meeting section through the origin.
title: A minimal critical mixed circuit has exact global cap flatness
